data.title: The FPGA turns 40
data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary: 这篇文章回顾了FPGA（现场可编程门阵列）技术过去40年的发展历程。1985年，Xilinx推出了首款商用FPGA——XC2064，具备64个可配置逻辑块。随着技术进步，现代FPGA如AMD旗下的高端产品，已拥有890万个系统逻辑单元，集成了Arm处理核心、多吉比特收发器、块内存、DSP元素等多种功能。FPGA的发展从简单的逻辑设计工具演变为支持高层次编程语言和自动布局布线的复杂系统，广泛应用于航空、汽车、数据中心等领域。文章还预告了2025年10月7日的英国FPGA会议，并介绍了相关培训课程和开发板资源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FPGA的现状、开源工具链、应用前景及相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• **支持开源FPGA工具链**：[transpute] 提到经过多年逆向工程，目前已有支持AMD/Xilinx 7系列芯片的开源FPGA工具链（如openxc7和f4pga.org）。该工具链支持多种FPGA，并与商业工具Vivado在资源使用和运行时间上形成对比，显示出开源工具的潜力。
  
• **质疑FPGA在通用计算中的地位**：[mikewarot] 认为FPGA中的路由结构在通用计算中是一种“过早优化”，并提出如果仅使用查找表构建计算阵列（如其BitGrid概念），可以节省大量硅片资源并提高效率。这与主流FPGA设计思路存在分歧。

• **FPGA市场与应用的局限性**：[avidiax] 指出，FPGA由于高昂的成本和ASIC替代的趋势，难以在规模化应用中持续存在。虽然FPGA具有动态重配置的优势，但在现有计算能力已经很强的情况下，其优势并不明显。

• **对FPGA工具链开放性的不满**：[amelius] 认为FPGA行业在开放源代码工具方面进展缓慢，40年来仍未广泛采用开源工具，暗示行业应更积极地拥抱开源。

• **FPGA在特定领域的优势**：[b0a04gl] 强调FPGA在低延迟、实时控制、硬件逻辑调整等特定领域中具有不可替代的优势，尤其是在高频交易、电信和云加速器等应用中，尽管最终设计稳定后可能会转向ASIC。

补充讨论：
• **FPGA价格和市场竞争**：[transpute] 提到通过中国分销商（如LCSC）可以以较低价格购买FPGA部件，这比通过传统渠道（如Digikey）便宜得多，暗示市场价格不透明性。[burnt-resistor] 回顾了FPGA历史，提到Xilinx和Altera（后被Intel收购）的竞争。

• **FPGA编程的易用性**：[fluorinerocket] 提到National Instruments通过LabVIEW使非电子工程师也能编程FPGA，但该技术被锁定在NI产品中，未能广泛推广。

• **FPGA在未来技术中的潜力**：[jumploops] 认为FPGA的硬件动态优化能力尚未完全实现，但可能在LLM（大语言模型）等未来技术中找到更多应用场景。[ge96] 则简单提到FPGA可能在AGI（人工通用智能）中有用。

争议焦点：
• FPGA在通用计算中的效率和地位：[mikewarot] 认为FPGA中的路由资源浪费，提出简化计算结构的观点，与其他评论者对FPGA在特定领域优势的肯定形成对比。
  
• FPGA工具链的开放性：[amelius] 对FPGA工具链封闭性表示不满，而[transpute] 则展示了开源工具链的进展，表明部分社区正在积极推动开源工具链的发展。

44333033.article_content:
Search
This year marks the 40th anniversary of one of the most exciting and interesting aspects of electronic engineering: the FPGA. The first commercially viable FPGA introduced in 1985 was the Xilinx XC2064, which provided developers with 64 configurable logic blocks, each with a three-input look-up tables.
From tiny acorns mighty OAK trees grow. Forty years later, the largest AMD (the successor to Xilinx) FPGA contains 8.9 million system logic cells, providing 8.2 million flip flops and 4 million look up tables, quite an increase on the original 64 LUTs.
It is not just the increase in CLBs and registers that distinguish modern FPGAs from their predecessors. Modern devices contain entire processing systems with a range of Arm® processing cores, multi giga bit transceivers, block memory, digital signal processing elements, memory controllers, AI acceleration capabilities and I/O cells which are exceptionally flexible and support a range of standards across single and differential interfaces.
Let’s take a look back at some of the very early days of FPGAs.
The XC2064 sold for $55, which is roughly equivalent to $165 in 2025. By the end of its commercial life 15 years later, it was available for $5 (or about $15 in today’s prices). The PCN announcing the XC2000 family discontinuation was announced in December 1996, with final deliveries in June 1999.
The introduction of the first FPGA led to a seismic shift in how electronic designers could create digital logic solutions. Pretty quickly, designs that had required a complete circuit board could be implemented within the XC2064 and its larger brother, the XC2018 (which offered 100 CLBs). Within two years of the XC2000 family being introduced, the XC3000 (1987)  was in production, which ranged from 64 CLBs to 484 CLBs in the largest. By 1989, the first million FPGA devices had been sold. Xilinx would go for an IPO a year later in 1990, and swiftly introduce it third FPGA family, the XC4000 in 1991. The XC4000XL from this family became the first 3v3 FPGAs.
The fourth generation of devices moved from numerical names to those that we are familiar with today: Virtex and Spartan, etc.
Programming these original FPGAs was very different to today. High level meant the ability to enter the design using Boolean expressions, Karnaugh maps or truth tables. Using Xilinx Design Editor (XDE), this enabled the designer to work with all of the logic and routing resources within the target device.
XDE was very much a physical design editor. As FPGAs became more viable and grew in capability, Xilinx wanted to enable developers to be able to leverage the time to market benefit of FPGAs. As such, they worked on development of logical to physical design and automatic place and route.
By 1996, around the time FPGAs were brought to my attention while at university, FPGAs resembled something a modern FPGA developer might recognise. They could be developed using HDLs, and provided MAP and Place and Route with implementation engines. IP cores with Core Generator were also starting to emerge. We were really off the starting blocks.
My first professional interaction with FPGAs was designing a Virtex-E M, which I talked about
here
. Since then, I have developed FPGAs for a wide range of applications, from submarines, to nuclear reactors, aerospace, defence, data centre, automotive, robotics and space. FPGAs play a large role in these and many other applications, and will for many years to come.

44333033.article_summary: 这篇文章回顾了FPGA（现场可编程门阵列）技术过去40年的发展历程。1985年，Xilinx推出了首款商用FPGA——XC2064，具备64个可配置逻辑块。随着技术进步，现代FPGA如AMD旗下的高端产品，已拥有890万个系统逻辑单元，集成了Arm处理核心、多吉比特收发器、块内存、DSP元素等多种功能。FPGA的发展从简单的逻辑设计工具演变为支持高层次编程语言和自动布局布线的复杂系统，广泛应用于航空、汽车、数据中心等领域。文章还预告了2025年10月7日的英国FPGA会议，并介绍了相关培训课程和开发板资源。
44333033.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FPGA的现状、开源工具链、应用前景及相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• **支持开源FPGA工具链**：[transpute] 提到经过多年逆向工程，目前已有支持AMD/Xilinx 7系列芯片的开源FPGA工具链（如openxc7和f4pga.org）。该工具链支持多种FPGA，并与商业工具Vivado在资源使用和运行时间上形成对比，显示出开源工具的潜力。
  
• **质疑FPGA在通用计算中的地位**：[mikewarot] 认为FPGA中的路由结构在通用计算中是一种“过早优化”，并提出如果仅使用查找表构建计算阵列（如其BitGrid概念），可以节省大量硅片资源并提高效率。这与主流FPGA设计思路存在分歧。

• **FPGA市场与应用的局限性**：[avidiax] 指出，FPGA由于高昂的成本和ASIC替代的趋势，难以在规模化应用中持续存在。虽然FPGA具有动态重配置的优势，但在现有计算能力已经很强的情况下，其优势并不明显。

• **对FPGA工具链开放性的不满**：[amelius] 认为FPGA行业在开放源代码工具方面进展缓慢，40年来仍未广泛采用开源工具，暗示行业应更积极地拥抱开源。

• **FPGA在特定领域的优势**：[b0a04gl] 强调FPGA在低延迟、实时控制、硬件逻辑调整等特定领域中具有不可替代的优势，尤其是在高频交易、电信和云加速器等应用中，尽管最终设计稳定后可能会转向ASIC。

补充讨论：
• **FPGA价格和市场竞争**：[transpute] 提到通过中国分销商（如LCSC）可以以较低价格购买FPGA部件，这比通过传统渠道（如Digikey）便宜得多，暗示市场价格不透明性。[burnt-resistor] 回顾了FPGA历史，提到Xilinx和Altera（后被Intel收购）的竞争。

• **FPGA编程的易用性**：[fluorinerocket] 提到National Instruments通过LabVIEW使非电子工程师也能编程FPGA，但该技术被锁定在NI产品中，未能广泛推广。

• **FPGA在未来技术中的潜力**：[jumploops] 认为FPGA的硬件动态优化能力尚未完全实现，但可能在LLM（大语言模型）等未来技术中找到更多应用场景。[ge96] 则简单提到FPGA可能在AGI（人工通用智能）中有用。

争议焦点：
• FPGA在通用计算中的效率和地位：[mikewarot] 认为FPGA中的路由资源浪费，提出简化计算结构的观点，与其他评论者对FPGA在特定领域优势的肯定形成对比。
  
• FPGA工具链的开放性：[amelius] 对FPGA工具链封闭性表示不满，而[transpute] 则展示了开源工具链的进展，表明部分社区正在积极推动开源工具链的发展。

data.title: FICO to incorporate buy-now-pay-later loans into credit scores
data.author: cebert
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：信用使用、信用评分系统及其影响

不同观点：
• PostOnce认为信用应该用于投资以提高生产力，而不是用于消费或延迟工作。他将信用视为一种时间交易工具，如果用于娱乐而非投资，最终会导致时间赤字和财务崩溃。
• Yizahi指出，信用本质上是增加债务负担的工具，并暗示其中可能存在腐败或游说行为。
• alkonaut讨论了在某些国家中，信用检查仅用于评估风险，而不像美国那样有明确的信用评分系统。他质疑将风险与商业机会混为一谈的合理性。
• segmondy担心如果没有使用“立即购买，稍后付款”（BNPL）的历史，可能会受到惩罚。
• OptionOfT指出BNPL通常只进行软检查，并质疑这种做法是否会改变。他还认为，按时支付不应影响信用评分。
• 9cb14c1ec0认为BNPL的流行是基于其被视为免费资金，而非实际信贷工具，最终会导致问题。
• jppope对BNPL的商业模式表示好奇，认为其可能在信用体系之外运作。
• seatac76认为对小额贷款的违约情况进行监控对金融市场稳定是有必要的。
• janalsncm询问BNPL和信用卡之间的功能性差异，并认为BNPL的流行可能与其简便的入门流程有关。
• eagerpace担心如果不使用BNPL，信用评分可能会下降。
• hk1337认为将BNPL纳入信用评分系统可能会鼓励财务 irresponsibility，并为贷款人提供新的拒绝贷款的理由。
• focusgroup0从历史角度提问，为什么某些传统禁止高利贷。
• firesteelrain简单预测信用评分将进一步下降。
• mihaaly关注信用评分系统带来的隐私和安全问题，认为敏感数据的收集和存储增加了个人风险。
• ecshafer认为新的信用评分标准主要会影响信用评分极低的人，高信用评分者不太可能使用BNPL。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了BNPL与传统信用卡的比较，包括其流行原因、使用便捷性及潜在风险。
• 隐私和安全问题被提出作为避免使用信用工具的一个理由，特别是在涉及敏感个人数据时。
• 争议的焦点在于信用评分系统的公平性及其对个人财务决策的影响，特别是在BNPL和其他小额贷款工具的普及下。

data.title: BYOK – Bring Your Own Keyboard
data.author: kevinbluer
data.article_summary: 文章宣布了一款名为"Device"的无干扰写作设备即将开始预售，供应有限，鼓励用户立即获取早期访问权。同时，文章还介绍了一个名为"Studio"的灵感写作平台。这两款产品旨在为写作者提供更好的写作体验，帮助他们专注于创作，减少干扰。预售即将开始，感兴趣的用户需尽快行动以确保获得早期访问机会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于无干扰写作设备的实用性、性价比和设计优劣的讨论。

不同观点：
• **支持使用简单工具替代无干扰设备**：[wenc] 认为不需要专门的无干扰写作设备，推荐使用钢笔和优质笔记本，或者将旧平板与折叠键盘组合使用，关闭无线网络并仅安装写作应用，如Google Docs。他还指出，电子墨水设备因刷新率低而不适合使用。
• **批评硬件与软件租赁模式**：[Workaccount2] 批评一些无干扰设备需要按月租赁软件，认为这种商业模式不合理，是对消费者的剥削。
• **质疑设备性价比**：[joeblubaugh] 和 [ryukoposting] 都提到，这些设备价格过高，功能有限，尤其是显示文本行数太少，性价比不如手机上的基本写作应用或二手笔记本电脑。
• **设备兼容性问题**：[dsr_] 指出，所谓的“通用键盘兼容性”名不副实，设备无法连接多种类型的键盘，如Mac键盘和PS/2接口的键盘。
• **设备实用性争议**：[KevinCarbonara] 认为这些设备只适合那些缺乏自制力的人，但购买设备并不能真正解决自控问题。同时，[Xevion] 和 [mnky9800n] 也认为这些设备是“为解决问题而制造的问题”，并非所有人都需要。
• **DIY替代方案**：[mavilia] 建议使用开源的ZeroWriter来实现类似的无干扰写作体验，而 [joshmarinacci] 则表示有意利用Raspberry Pico制作类似设备，特别是加入电子墨水屏幕以延长电池寿命。
• **显示屏尺寸问题**：[mwambua] 和 [ryukoposting] 都提到，这些设备的屏幕太小，无法方便地浏览之前写的内容，影响写作体验。

补充讨论：
• **设备设计与功能改进建议**：[rickcarlino] 建议在产品页面上添加设备照片以帮助理解，[voidhorse] 则对设备的云管理和文档处理功能表示不满，认为应该提供更多备份选项，而不是强制使用厂商的云服务。
• **无干扰理念的反思**：[SideburnsOfDoom] 指出，无干扰设备只是将干扰问题从软件转移到了硬件上，但并不能完全消除干扰，因为用户仍然可能被其他设备（如手机）分心。

争议焦点：
• 无干扰写作设备是否真的必要，以及它们的性价比和功能设计是否合理。
• 硬件与软件租赁模式的合理性以及设备兼容性问题。

data.title: Scientists use bacteria to turn plastic waste into paracetamol
data.author: bdev12345
data.article_summary: 科学家发现可以通过基因改造的大肠杆菌将塑料废料转化为扑热息痛（对乙酰氨基酚），开辟了一种更可持续的药物生产方式。目前，扑热息痛主要从石油中提取。研究团队利用聚对苯二甲酸乙二醇酯（PET）塑料，通过化学方法将其转化为新材料，再由改造后的大肠杆菌利用该材料通过生物化学反应生产出扑热息痛。该过程利用了洛森重排反应，且在细胞内由磷酸盐催化完成。该技术不仅能减少塑料污染，还能降低药物生产的碳排放，具有重要的应用潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用大肠杆菌将PET塑料转化为对乙酰氨基酚（acetaminophen）的研究及其相关讨论

不同观点：
• [tux3] 认为该研究的核心发现——Lossen重排反应不会杀死大肠杆菌——并不是特别新颖。他质疑为什么不直接进行Lossen反应，再将产物提供给细菌处理，并指出文中的描述让人误以为这是一个将塑料神奇地转化为小分子的全新过程，但实际上这些步骤早已存在。

• [casey2] 对该类科技创新持批评态度，认为与其关注这些“创新表演”故事，不如更多关注如何减少塑料生产以解决塑料废物问题。他的观点反映了对科技创新在解决环境问题上的实际效用的怀疑。

• [aduwah] 通过分享一个末世主题的视频链接，暗示当前的塑料污染问题可能导致严重后果，表达了对环境问题的担忧，但没有直接讨论研究本身。

• [lawlessone] 以半开玩笑的方式提出，是否可以通过mRNA疫苗的方式让人的身体能够分解塑料，暗示对科技能解决此类问题的期望或讽刺。

The discovery opens up the possibility of a more sustainable process for producing paracetamol, which ‘currently comes from oil’.
Photograph: Allison Dinner/EPA
View image in fullscreen
The discovery opens up the possibility of a more sustainable process for producing paracetamol, which ‘currently comes from oil’.
Photograph: Allison Dinner/EPA
Drugs
Scientists use bacteria to turn plastic waste into paracetamol
Genetically modified E coli
used to create painkillers from material produced from plastic bottles
Nicola Davis
Science correspondent
Mon 23 Jun 2025 11.00 EDT
Last modified on Mon 23 Jun 2025 18.06 EDT
Share
Bacteria can be used to turn plastic waste into painkillers, researchers have found, opening up the possibility of a more sustainable process for producing the drugs.
Chemists have discovered E coli can be used to create paracetamol, also known as acetaminophen, from a material produced in the laboratory from plastic bottles.
“People don’t realise that paracetamol comes from oil currently,” said Prof Stephen Wallace, the lead author of the research from the University of
Edinburgh
. “What this technology shows is that by merging chemistry and biology in this way for the first time, we can make paracetamol more sustainably and clean up plastic waste from the environment at the same time.”
Writing in the journal Nature Chemistry,
Wallace and colleagues report how they discovered that a type of chemical reaction called a Lossen rearrangement, a process that has never been seen in nature, was biocompatible. In other words, it could be carried out in the presence of living cells without harming them.
The team made their discovery when they took polyethylene terephthalate (PET) – a type of plastic often found in food packaging and bottles – and, using sustainable chemical methods, converted it into a new material.
When the researchers incubated this material with a harmless strain of E coli they found it was converted into another substance known as Paba in a process that must have involved a Lossen rearrangement.
Crucially, while the Lossen rearrangement typically involves harsh laboratory conditions, it occurred spontaneously in the presence of the E coli, with the researchers discovering it was catalysed by phosphate within the cells themselves.
The team add that Paba is an essential substance that bacteria need for growth, in particular the synthesis of DNA, and is usually made within the cell from other substances. However, the E coli used in the experiments was genetically modified to block these pathways, meaning the bacteria had to use the PET-based material.
The researchers say the results are exciting as they suggest plastic waste can be converted into biological material.
“It is a way to just completely hoover up plastic waste,” said Wallace.
The researchers then genetically modified the E coli further, inserting two genes – one from mushrooms and one from soil bacteria – that enabled the bacteria to convert PABA into paracetamol.
The team say that by using this form of E coli they were able to turn the PET-based starting material into paracetamol in under 24 hours, with low emissions and a yield of up to 92%.
While further work would be needed to produce paracetamol in this way at commercial levels, the results could have a practical application.
“It enables, for the first time, a pathway from plastic waste to paracetamol, which is not possible using biology alone, and it’s not possible using chemistry alone,” Wallace said.

data.title: How many PhDs does world need? Doctoral graduates outnumber academia jobs
data.author: TMWNN
data.article_summary: 全球博士毕业生数量在过去几十年持续增长，尤其在中国和印度迅速增加。2023年，中国有超过60万名博士生在读。然而，博士毕业生数量远超学术机构的岗位空缺，许多博士生面临激烈的学术职位竞争。同时，越来越多博士毕业生在非学术领域就业，可能与其专业不对口或不理想。在南非，18%的博士毕业生难以找到相关工作。尽管如此，总体职业满意度较高，尤其是科技领域的博士生。教育专家呼吁博士教育应更具意义，并与社会和劳动力市场的多样化需求更好对接。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：博士毕业生数量与学术职位数量不匹配的问题，以及博士教育的目的和职业导向。

不同观点：
• **dekhn**：20世纪90年代末，克林顿增加了NIH的预算，导致培训资助大幅增加，博士项目得以扩展。然而，教授职位并未相应增加，许多博士不得不寻找其他职业。这反而让大科技公司受益，吸收了这些具有强大技能（如机器学习）的前物理学家等人才。

• **lapcat**：大学利用研究生作为廉价劳动力进行教学和研究，因此大学有动力招收超过学术职位数量的学生，导致供需失衡。

• **bwfan123**：即使是爱因斯坦在获得博士学位后也没有立即获得学术职位，表明即使是顶尖人才也会面临学术就业困难，因此博士生应为学术界外的职业做好准备。

• **streptomycin**：对于不想进入学术界的研究生，选择具有行业经验的博士导师是个好主意，他们能提供在行业内成功的必要指导和人脉，尤其在工程领域可能更容易找到这样的导师。

• **Simulacra**：只要有学生愿意支付学费和政府支持贷款，大学就会不断吸引学生投入时间和金钱，即使最终职业前景不明朗。过去获得博士学位可能更困难，但现在供需失衡问题更加突出。

• **Apreche**：许多行业都存在类似问题，比如动画行业。建议学术机构根据雇主需求而非学生需求来驱动，停止对学生隐瞒职业现实。应让各行业告知大学所需的劳动力类型，并据此调整招生人数，以免学生浪费多年时间和金钱。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于大学是否在利用研究生作为廉价劳动力，以及博士教育是否应更加面向行业需求。
• 讨论中也提到了现实例子（如爱因斯坦）和跨行业比较（如动画行业）来支持观点，强调博士生需为学术界外职业做好准备。
• 有人提出导师的行业经验对博士生的职业发展至关重要，尤其是在工程等领域。

More than 600,000 students were enrolled in PhD programmes in China in 2023.
Credit: ChinaImages/Sipa USA via Alamy
The number of doctoral graduates globally has been growing steadily over the past few decades. And in countries such as China and India, those numbers are exploding.
Conventionally, the doctorate was a stepping stone to a lifelong career in academia. But today, the number of PhD graduates vastly exceeds the number of job openings at universities and research institutions. Researchers say that many universities are not preparing graduates for a career outside academia.
“We need to make doctoral education more meaningful, more sustainable and better aligned with the diverse societal and labour-market needs,” says Cláudia Sarrico, the Secretary of State for Higher Education in Portugal, who previously worked at the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) in Paris.
The PhD explosion
Among the 38 countries belonging to the OECD, the number of new doctorate holders almost doubled between 1998 and 2017
1
, and has continued to increase in the years since. (Although
several countries
, including Australia and Brazil, have seen a dip in PhD enrolments over the past few years, driven in part by high living costs and low stipends.)
In China, the number of doctoral students has doubled — from around 300,000 in 2013 to more than 600,000 students enrolled in PhD programmes in 2023. “The numbers are massive, and they keep growing,” says Hugo Horta, who researches higher-education policy and practice at the University of Hong Kong. There are several factors driving this growth, Horta explains, such as the increasing number of people with bachelor’s and master’s degrees, and the expectation among many in the country that an investment in higher education will provide better economic and social prospects.
But the number of jobs in academia has not kept pace with the growth in PhD holders, says Horta. People coming into these doctoral programmes are, for the most part, training to become academics, so many future graduates are going to face fierce competition for any position, he says.
Great expectations
In countries such as the United States, Australia and the United Kingdom, non-academic jobs are increasingly becoming the norm for people with PhDs. A 2023 study
2
of more than 4,500 PhD graduates in the United Kingdom found that over two-thirds of doctoral graduates were employed outside academia.
Such employment can mean graduates taking jobs that aren’t research based or that are outside their area of expertise. In South Africa, out of more than 6,000 PhD graduates who completed a 2020 survey,
18% said that they had had trouble finding jobs related to their expertise
. “Even though they do find jobs, it’s not necessarily linked to their PhDs, and it’s not always the jobs that they expected or that they wanted,” says Milandré van Lill, a researcher at Stellenbosch University in South Africa and a co-author of the study. “From my perspective, we have reached saturation point in terms of PhD graduates.” Some graduates who find jobs outside of academia feel overqualified and undervalued, says van Lill.
That isn’t the case everywhere. The 2023 study found that job satisfaction among PhD graduates was generally high, with more than 90% saying they were happy with their career
2
. Those in science- and technology-related fields were more likely to find research-related roles — which are linked to higher levels of job satisfaction — than were those in the social sciences, arts and humanities.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：计算机科学（CS）毕业生的就业情况和当前就业市场变化的原因及影响

不同观点：
• Workaccount2认为，当前CS毕业生的就业市场变化并非由人工智能（AI）引起，而是因为几年前学生选择专业时，编程工作因多种因素变得非常理想，导致目前初级岗位工资低，以此筛选出真正有热情的人。
• paxys指出，CS毕业生的就业不足率最低，与其他专业（如艺术史）的毕业生不同，CS毕业生通常会坚持寻找专业对口的工作，并因此获得高薪。
• carls提醒大家注意，讨论中的数据是来自2023年，可能需要考虑数据的时间性。
• dr_kiszonka认为，对于接近总体失业率的个位数百分比差异，不必过于担心，虽然数据值得思考，但现在恐慌还为时过早。
• poulsbohemian指出，当前情况是否是暂时现象或系统性问题需要时间验证，并提到在互联网泡沫破裂后，新毕业生经历了几年的挣扎，有些人从未真正找到立足点，过去十年是一个就业和薪酬的异常时期。
• pyuser583提醒大家，CS专业并不一定意味着毕业生都是合格的程序员。
• gamblor956提供了纽约联邦储备银行研究报告的链接，指出中期职业工资对所有职业来说都低得令人惊讶。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于当前CS就业市场变化的原因（AI影响 vs. 历史因素）以及这种变化是否是暂时性或系统性的。
• 数据的时间性和准确性也被提及，强调需要更长期的数据来做出更准确的判断。
• CS毕业生的质量和能力问题也被提出，表明并非所有CS毕业生都能轻松找到高薪工作。

data.title: China's Many Ghost Towns of Abandoned Mansions (2024)
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 中国幽灵城市问题日益严重，许多豪华房地产项目因各种原因被迫停工，成为废弃的“鬼城”。例如，位于沈阳的“国宾府”项目原本计划为社会精英建造宫殿式别墅，但在2010年开工后仅两年便停工，留下数百栋未完成的仿皇家别墅，如今被用作牧场，牛群在别墅间活动。这些废弃建筑反映了中国房地产市场的深层危机，恒大集团等大型开发商因债务问题破产，导致大量楼盘烂尾。中国的人口老龄化、房价负担问题以及疫情等因素加剧了供需失衡，进一步打击了市场信心。这一现象不仅影响房地产行业，也对整体经济构成风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：房地产开发中的问题及不同国家的对比

不同观点：

China’s ghost cities are far more common than one might think. Take the State Guest Mansions, a development envisioned as the palatial homes for the upper crust of society. Now their only residents are hurdles of cattle and the occasional adventure explorers meandering like ghosts around the arched verandas and stone façades of hundreds of abandoned villas. Located around the hills of Shenyang (about 400 miles northeast of Beijing), the development was originally planned by Greenland Group, a
Shanghai
-based real estate developer, and broke ground in 2010. But as
AFP
reports, within two years, the project had come to a grinding halt, leaving the half-formed skeletons of imitative royalty in its wake. Today the crumbling estates are still abandoned, left in an eerie series of rows appearing like an architectural cornfield.
Makeshift pens corral cattle and other farm animals.
Photo: Jade Gao/AFP/Getty Images
The irony of this formation will only grow more apparent as the seasons begin to turn, as local farmers have begun plowing the land between villas for future crops. Would-be garages of the abandoned mansions are now repurposed as storage for hay bails, and modest two-rail fences corral herds of cows between properties.
A model of the development is seen in the sales center.
Photo: Jade Gao/AFP/Getty Images
Developers had already made significant progress on the homes when the project was abandoned.
Photo: Jade Gao/AFP/Getty Images
The interiors of the abandoned mansions are perhaps even more poignant. A heavy layer of dust and scraps of garbage are the only furnishing in the rooms, a stark contrast to what appears to be marble floors and columns, crystal chandeliers, coffered ceilings, and intricate marquetry. In what would have been the sales center, a model of the completed 260-villa neighborhood still sits. “These (homes) would have sold for millions—but the rich haven’t even bought one of them,” a farmer named Guo told AFP.
The plowed fields of the development were originally expected to be the verdant gardens of the homeowners.
Photo: Jade Gao/AFP/Getty Images
A broader real estate crisis
The State Guest Mansions are are just a number of deserted developments scattered around China, an occurrence that speaks to a growing real estate crisis in the country. Nearby is an abandoned high-rise complex, which Jonathan Cheng, a reporter for the the
Wall Street Journal,
visited in February 2024 and
documented in a video
on the paper’s website. “This is just another of the residential property developments in Shenyang that have frozen in their tracks,” Cheng says, pointing at a collection of dozens of roughly 15-story buildings. With concrete frames and nonexistent windows, the buildings look like empty oversized Brutalist doll houses waiting for someone to come sprinkle life into their interiors.
But like a toy cast aside long after a child grows up, it’s unlikely that the project will get picked up again. The complex was developed by China Evergrande Group, the country’s biggest residential real estate developer, which
filed for bankruptcy
in August 2023. This January, a Hong Kong court ordered the
company to liquidate
, as it was unable to restructure the $300 billion that it owes to investors. According to the
Wall Street Journal
,
about 800,000 of the company’s 1.2 million presold units remain unfinished.
Another abandoned development in Huangshan, China
Photo: Zhang Peng/LightRocket/Getty Images
What is causing China’s real estate problem?
China’s ghost cities represent a major problem with the country’s real estate market. For decades, China’s economy was driven by real estate, so much so that the government often encouraged large-scale developments. But an
aging population, affordability concerns
, and the COVID-19 pandemic, among other factors, resulted in a supply-demand imbalance. Further, the Chinese government has been increasingly cracking down on developers’
reckless borrowing habits
.
Forest City in Malaysia is largely empty, despite being planned to house 700,000 people.
Photo: Aparna Nori/Bloomberg/Getty Images
Evergrande’s collapse is just the most notable example of an occurrence that is happening all across China. Numerous developers are massively in debt, defaulting on payments, and struggling with losses, resulting in these unfinished housing projects and skeletal would-be communities. Greenland Group, the developer responsible for the State Guest Mansion, recently defaulted on $400 million worth of international bonds, Chen reported in the video. These issues have also caused many middle-class Chinese citizens to lose faith in the real estate market, further impacting demand and creating additional risks for the country’s broader economy. As
Bloomberg
reports, many citizens have grown wealth through real estate, and 70% of family assets are stored in property. “Every 5% decline in home prices will wipe out 19 trillion yuan ($2.7 trillion) in hou

data.title: Pixar's Newest Movie, 'Elio', Is a Box-Office Dud
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：原创电影在影院的吸引力、宣传力度、发行方式及市场表现

不同观点：
• [paxys] 认为如今电影票价过高，观众只愿意为大IP续作（如《速度与激情》和《玩具总动员》）买单，导致市场上缺乏原创电影。高票价使得观众对失望的观影体验容忍度降低。
  
• [thcipriani] 表示自己偶然发现了原创电影《Elio》，虽然影片质量不错，但几乎没有宣传，自己是在寻找电影时偶然看到的。相比之下，重制版和续集电影的宣传力度更大。

• [rocketvole] 指出，票房不再是衡量电影成功的唯一标准，流媒体播放量正变得越来越重要。这也是为什么许多大制片厂更愿意制作直接上线流媒体的电影，例如索尼的《Kpop Demon Hunters》。

• [NBJack] 表示《Elio》的预告片和制作团队之前的作品（如《寻梦环游记》《恐龙当家》）并不吸引他，尤其是配音演员布拉德·加勒特的声线不太适合角色。

• [joeblubaugh] 认为《Elio》对四岁孩子非常友好，但自己也是偶然了解到这部电影，最初是在寻找《28年后》的发行日期时发现的。

• [archerx] 批评《Elio》的3D CalArts风格让人反感，认为这种设计是一种倒退，远不如早期皮克斯角色设计出色。

• [snarkyturtle] 认为《Elio》在《星际宝贝》和《驯龙高手》等大片仍在热映时上映是不明智的，尤其是《星际宝贝》全球票房已经突破9亿美元。

• [jessyco] 提到自己完全没有听说过《Elio》，也没有在YouTube、电台或朋友中看到任何宣传。

• [andrewmcwatters] 对“皮克斯电影完全在美国制作，导致成本增加”的说法表示不满，认为这是在为高成本找借口。

• [Spivak] 指出在Disney+上，《Elio》的推荐位置并不显眼，排在《冰雪奇缘》和《蜘蛛侠》之后，令人意外，毕竟这是一部投资2.5亿美元的电影。

补充讨论：
• 宣传不足是多位评论者共同关注的问题，许多人表示通过偶然的机会才了解到《Elio》。
• 不同观众对电影的风格和配音有不同看法，特别是对3D设计和配音演员的选择存在争议。
• 流媒体的兴起被认为是传统影院发行模式的挑战，制片厂更愿意选择直接上线流媒体的发行方式。
• 高票价和市场对大IP续作的偏好使得原创电影在影院中难以获得成功。

data.title: High levels of toxic chemicals found in paper receipts used by US retailers
data.author: jmsflknr
data.article_summary: 新研究发现，美国多家零售商的购物小票含有高水平的有毒化学物质——双酚S（BPS），接触10秒即可超过加州的安全标准。双酚S与癌症和生殖问题有关，特别对收银员等长时间接触小票的人危害更大。环保组织CEH已向约50家零售商发出违规通知，包括Burger King、Chanel、Dollar General等，要求停止使用含BPS的小票或贴上警告标识。若企业未在60天内回应，CEH将提起诉讼。消费者可通过拒收小票或选择电子小票自我保护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：收据的毒性及其处理方式

不同观点：
• mrangle 认为收据的毒性问题应得到重视，并建议制定相关法律进行管理。其论据是收据的毒性不为大众所知，甚至连收银员也可能不了解。此外，mrangle 还提到人们对于接触报纸的合理性也缺乏意识。
• more_corn 对此持嘲讽态度，认为使用环保标签的超市也在使用有害的热敏纸打印收据，指出收据是交易过程中最具毒性的部分，且消费者往往不需要或不想要这些收据。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于收据的毒性是否被充分认识以及是否有必要通过法律手段加以管理。
• more_corn 的评论暗示了对某些自称环保的商家使用不环保材料的讽刺，反映了商业实践与环保主张之间的矛盾。
• mrangle 提到了更广泛的公共意识问题，包括对其他日常物品（如报纸）的潜在毒性的忽视。

44359406.article_content:
Dollar General is among a group of retailers found to have a toxic chemical in paper receipts according to new research.
Photograph: Brandon Bell/Getty Images
View image in fullscreen
Dollar General is among a group of retailers found to have a toxic chemical in paper receipts according to new research.
Photograph: Brandon Bell/Getty Images
California
This article is more than
2 months old
High levels of toxic chemicals found in paper receipts used by US retailers
This article is more than 2 months old
Holding the receipts for 10 seconds absorbs enough bisphenol S to break California’s safety rule, research finds
Sign up for the Detox Your Kitchen newsletter
Tom Perkins
Mon 14 Apr 2025 06.00 EDT
Last modified on Mon 14 Apr 2025 08.41 EDT
Share
Paper receipts from major retailers in the US are so laden with bisphenol S that holding one for 10 seconds can cause the skin to absorb enough of the highly toxic chemical to violate California’s safety threshold, new research has found.
The findings are being used as evidence in
legal action
aimed at pressuring retailers to stop using receipt paper treated with bisphenol S, or BPS, which is
linked to
cancer and reproductive problems.
The Center for Environmental
Health
(CEH) non-profit has sent violation notices to about 50 major retailers alerting them to the exceedance of California’s Proposition 65 limits for BPS.
Among the companies to which
notices
were sent for the allegedly illegal levels of BPS in their receipts are Burger King, Chanel, Dollar General, AMC Theaters, GameStop, Subway, Foot Locker and Ace Hardware.
“[The findings were] really eye-opening for us,” Mihir Vohra, science lead at the CEH, said. “They really speak to just how high the concentrations of BPS are in these receipts.”
Bisphenol is a class of chemicals used in a wide range of consumer products, such as food packaging, fabrics, toys and cookware. Regulators have largely focused on bisphenol A (BPA), which is banned in Europe for food uses because it is so toxic. Many companies have phased out BPA’s use and food companies often advertise when their packaging is BPA free.
But recent research has found BPS, the alternative largely used in place of BPA, to be
just as toxic
. It’s linked to hormone disruption, cognitive damage, decreased sperm count, breast cancer and other health issues.
Previous research has found it can be absorbed by the skin, and CEH’s new study shows how high the risk is just for brief exposures while holding a receipt. The findings are particularly concerning for cashiers and people working in retail who may handle many receipts throughout the day.
The CEH also noted that people in restaurants often hold receipts for a long period of time while looking at a bill or waiting for service.
The chemicals are added as a coating to thermal paper to help ink develop. Some alternatives exist, but many are also toxic, and the non-profit is urging companies to use something safe to avoid “playing Whac-a-Mole” with dangerous chemicals, said Kizzy Charles-Guzman, the CEH’s executive director. Some paper is
treated with vitamin C
, but the receipts aren’t as bright.

The violation notices give companies 60 days to respond. They will either have to switch to paper that does not include BPS or affix a warning to the products. That could potentially include a sign near a cash register that alerts consumers to the receipts’ toxicity.
If companies don’t respond within 60 days, the CEH can sue in California state court under Proposition 65 and ask a judge to order companies to use an alternative or provide a warning.
People can protect themselves by not taking a receipt or asking for an email receipt.

data.title: Skip the exit interview when you leave your job
data.author: ohjeez
data.article_summary: 在离职面谈中，避免抱怨前公司或同事。离职时应专注于留下好印象，不说负面言论，只需表示找到了新机会并感激曾有的工作经历。抱怨不会带来任何好处，反而可能损害你的声誉并树敌。HR可能会声称面谈内容保密，但这不一定可信。若对公司有建议，应在在职时提出，离职时说为时已晚且无益。关键是避免得罪人，保持 gracious 的离职态度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：离职面谈中是否应该给出诚实的反馈，以及这样做的利弊。

不同观点：
• charlie-83：认为可以在不破坏关系的情况下提供反馈。分享了自己在离职面谈中坦诚交流的正面经验，强调了反馈对留下同事的潜在帮助，以及可能留下的好印象。
• jrsdav：分享了一次给出负面反馈后导致领导层变动的情况，虽然被称为"传奇"，但担心可能因此破坏了一些关系，并表示时间会证明这种做法的影响。
• ironchef：认为在离职面谈中发言没有好处，可能被视为抱怨者，并可能树敌。但同时也承认如果反馈能改善朋友的工作环境，可以视为正面效果。
• akdor1154：批评将职场互动视为博弈论的做法，认为这是不愿意面对问题的原因，表达了对美国公司文化的不满。
• pxx：在离职面谈中只提到薪酬问题，结果公司后来做出了调整。认为直接指出关键问题可能带来改变。
• jonplackett：反对将所有公司人员视为无情 corporate 混蛋，指出很多公司中的人其实关心问题。
• m101：认为诚实的离职面谈是一种自由的行使，不诚实则是对未来雇主的屈服。
• moomin：描述了一次痛苦但无效的离职面谈经历，认为一旦辞职，离职面谈没有 upside，微笑离开是最好的选择。
• mianos：分享了自己在离职时尽力帮助团队的经验，但公司高层并不关心，认为这反映了公司文化问题。
• throwawaymaths：认为在小型初创公司中，诚实反馈有助于公司改进，特别是如果自己仍持有股份。
• zug_zug：认为坦率地表达意见是生活中的乐趣，比没有意见的 toxic 工作关系更有价值。
• mistermaster1：质疑离职面谈的实际效果，但随后分享了自己的经验，表明诚实反馈导致了不良经理的离职。
• potato3732842：支持反馈可以带来改变的观点，提到一次团队大量流失人才导致不良经理被解雇的案例。
• YmiYugy：认为不应一概而论，与 HR 交流时可以使用 corporate 语言，但如果与关系良好的经理或同事交流，诚实意见可能更有益。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于离职面谈中诚实反馈的利弊权衡，特别是对个人职业关系的影响。
• 一些人认为诚实反馈可以带来积极变化，而另一些人则担心树敌和职业风险。
• 经验的多样性反映了不同公司文化对离职面谈反馈的接受程度。
• 讨论中也涉及到职场关系的复杂性以及如何在离职时维护或破坏这些关系。

44360806.article_content:
« How to talk in an interview about problems at your past job without coming off as a complainer
The best open source project for someone might not be yours, and that's OK »
When it’s time to leave your job, someone from Human Resources may want to sit you down and have an “exit interview”. They’ll ask you questions like “Why are you leaving your position?” and “What was it like to work with your manager.” It’s done with this premise that they’re looking to make the company better.
Don’t take the bait. Say nothing negative about anyone or anything. Tell them that you’ve found another opportunity that you need to take, and that it’s been a privilege to work with them all. And that’s it.
Here’s why: There is absolutely no benefit for you to gain by talking in an exit interview, and plenty of negative consequences to come out of it. At best you’ll be remembered as a complainer, and you may make enemies.
As I wrote in my book
“Land The Tech Job You Love”
Once you’ve given your resignation, your goal until you leave the company is to be well remembered. You want people to say “Ol’ Steve, he was a good guy.” Leave graciously, and burn no bridges.
No matter how much you may enjoy the thought of telling your boss just how stupid he is, how poorly he runs the department, and how you can’t wait to hear how they’ll manage without you, keep it as a thought. There’s no good outcome of your actions, and they can only hurt you. Sending a long, rambling email telling your soon-to-be-ex co-workers about how you’re glad to be leaving is pointless and destructive.
People have long memories. We work in an extremely well-connected industry. Send a letter complaining about how terrible the company is, and that’s how you’ll be remembered. Everything good you’ve done will be eclipsed by your noisy departure. Chances are it will get around.
HR may assure you that everything that you say in your interview will be strictly confidential. This is a fiction or a fantasy, depending on how much the person in HR believes it. Plus, when you manager gets sent to sensitivity training a month after you leave, how hard is it for him to put two and two together?
Nobody wants to make an enemy. You may think you’ll never have to deal with the people you speak badly of again, but it’s an awfully small world out there.
Sometimes people say that “Well, how will the company get any better?” I suggest that that’s no longer your concern, and that the time for that has passed anyway. If you’re unhappy enough with the company to leave, then they’ve been doing things wrong for the duration of your employment.
What do you imagine will happen as a result of your exit interview? That the company that you need to get away from will magically pull its head of its ass? “Damn shame that Jenkins left, but I’m glad he told us about what a bad manager his boss was. Once we got rid of that guy, the world became a better place around here.” It won’t happen.
If you have suggestions on how things should work differently at the company, the time to tell your boss is while you work there. If they can’t bring themselves to act on it during your tenure, telling them at the exit interview isn’t going to do any good.
Again, the key here is that there is no potential upside for you. The best you can hope for is to not piss someone off. The potential negatives are great.
When the time comes for the exit interview, tell them you’ve found another opportunity that you need to take, and that you’re grateful for having had the chance to work at the company.  Be gracious and well-remembered as you leave.

NO WAY
SAN JOSE
Getty Images
Just because Silicon Valley is pumped to make this junk doesn’t mean people will buy it
Big Tech is fixated on making computers for your face and portable AI companions. Turns out there may be bad ideas in brainstorming.
Rani Molla
5/28/25 1:03PM
For all its innovation, it can sometimes feel like all of Big Tech coalesces along a single idea. Lately it’s seemed like Silicon Valley’s best idea for the
next best thing
has been the
same thing
: an AI-powered device that isn’t a phone.
Last week, OpenAI
announced
that it’s buying io, former
Apple
design lead Jony Ive’s AI hardware startup. The
plan
so far is to make a “companion” device that sits on your desk, in your pocket, or maybe
around your neck
, and works in addition to your phone or computer.
Most everyone else has settled on AI-powered smart glasses as the device du jour.
Apple itself
plans to release its AI-enhanced glasses
at the end of next year. Like its competitors, the device would have cameras, microphones, and speakers allowing it to assess the outside world and let users communicate with its voice assistant.
Last week,
Google
announced Android XR
, a framework meant to bring AI to face computers, including those made by Samsung,
Warby Parker
, and Gentle Monster.
Amazon has been working on AI glasses for
internal
use that would provide turn-by-turn navigation within buildings to help it decrease delivery times.
Meta
, which partnered with Ray-Ban owner EssilorLuxottica, is the furthest along, having already sold more than 2 million units since they came out in October 2023. The company says it
expects to produce 10 million a year
starting next year and is expected to offer a
more deluxe, more expensive
version of the glasses by the end of 2025.
The idea is all roughly the same: create a new form factor through which you can interact with AI. It’s meant to give users access to their phone without having to pick it up and to overlay useful information on the outside world. But it all raises some important questions.
Why is everyone having the same idea at the same time?
It’s easy to see why Big Tech companies might want this. Anything that enables them to sell you devices or services, serve you ads, collect data, and generally be closer to your everyday lives is a big win for them.
And the tech is more ready for prime time than it’s ever been.
“With Google Glass, when they first came out, everybody was creeped out”
While the general idea of AI glasses has been floating around since before Google’s first foray with Glass more than a decade ago, with the rise of generative AI and other advances, we’re much closer now to having the technology to make it actually work. AI is better able to correctly identify what you’re looking at, chips are more powerful, and batteries are smaller.
Society, too, is more ready.
“With Google Glass, when they first came out, everybody was creeped out that all of a sudden there’s potentially somebody with a camera on you all the time,” Counterpoint Technology senior analyst Gerrit Schneemann told Sherwood News. “But now with social media, the mainstream user is more aware of the constant nature of being potentially on camera, so there’s less of a friction there.”
It’s also possible that a separate AI device is a genuinely good idea. In other words, a type of
carcinization
is going on where the form factor is so useful that a number of unrelated things are evolving to look like it (and it’s not just tech companies wanting you to use their proverbial crab).
While much of what these smart devices are offering is already possible on your phone, glasses or other hands-free devices open up a world of possibilities.
“If you look at insert company here —  it could be Google, it could be Meta, it could be Microsoft or Apple or Jony Ive, etc. — there is a recognition of the potential conveniences that are unique to this device that you can’t get anywhere else,” Ramon Llamas, a research director at IDC who specializes in wearables, told Sherwood.
The companies themselves are quick to advertise
use cases for these devices.
As Shahram Izadi, vice president of AR/XR at Google, spun it at
Google’s developer conference
last week, “Unlike Clark Kent, you can get superpowers when you put your glasses on.”
Those powers were included in a demo where Product Manager Nishtha Bhatia  sent and received texts without her hands and instead used those hands to double high-five basketball player Giannis Antetokounmpo. She asked her glasses to look up a band and then play songs from that band. The glasses recalled a logo from her coffee cup earlier, made a calendar invite with someone at that coffee shop, and provided step-by-step directions to the coffee shop. Perhaps most impressive: with only a small glitch, Bhatia and Izadi were able to see real-time translations of what each person was saying in Hindi and Farsi, respectively.
Remember, of course, that demos at tech conferences are not real life.

data.title: Is mathematics mostly chaos or mostly order?
data.author: baruchel
data.article_summary:
文章探讨了数学中无限的本质，聚焦于两位数学家Juan Aguilera、Joan Bagaria和Philipp Lücke提出的两种新无限概念。传统上，无限被分为不同大小的“基数”，这些大基数形成了一个有序的层级体系。然而，新提出的两种无限基数打破了这一秩序，展现出一种“爆炸性”行为，带来了数学中更多的混沌。

一些学者如Toby Meadows认为这是数学进步的标志，而另一些如Hugh Woodin则持怀疑态度。大多数数学家使用ZFC公理体系，不常涉及这些深奥的无限问题。文章指出，数学的无限领域充满未知和不确定性，传统公理在此可能失效，新公理的提出也面临挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数学的本质及其属性（秩序与混沌、发现与构造、无限性）

不同观点：
• **数学是人类构造的产物**：metalman 认为数学是人类构造的，像秩序与混沌一样，其定义和使用随历史不断演变。人类无法指出一个有序的框架来解释宇宙，且在探讨深奥问题时应保持谨慎，因为答案可能带来意想不到的后果。

• **数学本质上是混沌的**：jerf 主张数学本质上是混沌的，有序的数学结构只是例外。大部分数学结构是无序且无法区分的，但那些有序的结构因其有趣和连贯性而值得研究。

• **数学与物理宇宙的类比**：danwills 提出数学宇宙可能像物理宇宙一样，由“暗物质”构成，这些不可见的东西可能是纯抽象的。尽管如此，抽象概念可以影响现实事物。danwills 还表达了对新发现的基数类型的兴趣。

• **对新无穷基数现象的质疑**：Sniffnoy 对文章中描述的新无穷基数“爆炸”现象提出质疑，指出在 ZFC 公理体系下，两个基数的和不可能出现这种现象，除非涉及无限和。

• **对康托尔对角线论证的困惑**：scrubs 表示对康托尔对角线论证的不解，尤其是涉及实数的列举和完成无穷大的概念，认为这些概念容易让人困惑。

• **数学发现的观点**：dgfitz 认为数学是发现的，而不是构造的或混沌的，它只是存在。数学发现是等待被找到的，而不是人为构造的。

• **对现代集合论的反思**：b0a04gl 质疑现代集合论是基于公理的反向工程，还是真正的发现。新的大基数理论可能打破了传统的叙事，暗示数学的无限性可能比我们想象的复杂。

• **非语言数学的倡导**：revskill 主张一种无语言的数学，所有意义都来自图形，认为如果不能用铅笔和圆规描述的意义就不算数。

• **秩序与混沌的关系**：lordfrito 认为秩序与混沌的关系才是关键，所有有趣的事情都发生在这两者的边界上，类似于计算中 0 和 1 的关系。

补充讨论：
• 对新基数类型和无穷性的兴趣在多个评论中被提及，显示出对这些新数学发现的关注和好奇心。
• 不同评论者对数学是发现还是构造的看法存在明显分歧，反映了哲学上的基本争论。
• 对康托尔对角线论证的困惑和现代集合论的反思表明，在高等数学中存在一些难以理解和争议的概念。
• 对秩序与混沌关系的讨论提供了一种综合视角，认为二者的互动是数学有趣和复杂的核心。

Is Mathematics Mostly Chaos or Mostly Order?
By
Gregory Barber
June 20, 2025
Two new notions of infinity challenge a long-standing plan to define the mathematical universe.
Comment
Save Article
Read Later
Mathematicians probe the boundaries of logic by inventing new types of infinity.
Wei-An Jin/
Quanta Magazine
Introduction
By
Gregory Barber
Contributing Writer
June 20, 2025
View PDF/Print Mode
foundations of mathematics
infinity
logic
mathematics
set theory
All topics
Last winter, at a meeting in the Finnish wilderness high above the Arctic Circle, a group of mathematicians gathered to contemplate the fate of a mathematical universe.
It was minus 20 degrees Celsius, and while some went cross-country skiing,
Juan Aguilera
, a set theorist at the Vienna University of Technology, preferred to linger in the cafeteria, tearing pieces of
pulla
pastry and debating the nature of two new notions of infinity. The consequences, Aguilera believed, were grand. “We just don’t know what they are yet,” he said.
Infinity, counterintuitively, comes in many shapes and sizes. This has been known since the 1870s, when the German mathematician Georg Cantor proved that the set of real numbers (all the numbers on the number line) is larger than the set of whole numbers, even though both sets are infinite. (The short version: No matter how you try to match real numbers to whole numbers, you’ll always end up with more real numbers.) The two sets, Cantor argued, represented entirely different flavors of infinity and therefore had profoundly different properties.
From there, Cantor constructed larger infinities, too. He took the set of real numbers, built a new set out of all of its subsets, then proved that this new set was bigger than the original set of real numbers. And when he took all the subsets of this new set, he got an even bigger set. In this way, he built infinitely many sets, each larger than the last. He referred to the different sizes of these infinite sets as cardinal numbers (not to be confused with the ordinary cardinals 1, 2, 3…).
Lucy Reading-Ikanda
Set theorists have continued to define cardinals that are far more exotic and difficult to describe than Cantor’s. In doing so, they’ve discovered something surprising: These “large cardinals” fall into a surprisingly neat hierarchy. They can be clearly defined in terms of size and complexity. Together, they form a massive tower of infinities that set theorists then use to probe the boundaries of what’s mathematically possible.
But the two new cardinals that Aguilera was pondering in the Arctic cold behaved oddly. He had
recently constructed them
, along with
Joan Bagaria
of the University of Barcelona and
Philipp Lücke
of the University of Hamburg, only to find that they didn’t quite fit into the usual hierarchy. Instead, they “exploded,” Aguilera said, creating a new class of infinities that their colleagues hadn’t bargained on — and implying that far more chaos abounds in mathematics than expected.
It’s a provocative claim. The prospect is, to some, exciting. “I love this paper,” said
Toby Meadows
, a logician and philosopher at the University of California, Irvine. “It seems like real progress — a really interesting insight that we didn’t have before.”
But it’s also difficult to really know whether the claim is true. That’s the nature of studying infinity. If mathematics is a tapestry sewn together by traditional assumptions that everyone agrees on, the higher reaches of the infinite are its tattered fringes. Set theorists working in these extreme areas operate in a space where the traditional axioms used to write mathematical proofs do not always apply, and where new axioms must be written — and often break down.
Up here, most questions are fundamentally unprovable, and uncertainty reigns. And so to some, the new cardinals don’t change anything. “I don’t buy it at all,” said
Hugh Woodin
, a set theorist at Harvard University who is currently leading the quest to fully define the mathematical universe. Woodin was Bagaria’s doctoral adviser 35 years ago and Aguilera’s in the 2010s. But his students are cutting their own path through infinity’s thickets. “Your children grow up and defy you,” Woodin said.
The Universes of Set Theory
Most mathematicians don’t concern themselves with these kinds of questions. They work with a set of nine assumptions, or axioms, about how sets behave, known as ZFC — “Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory with the axiom of choice.” These nine rules can’t be proved. Mathematicians have simply agreed that they provide a natural foundation for the rest of mathematics. From them, mathematicians build up rigorous proofs of all their conjectures.
Kurt Gödel showed that some reaches of mathematics will forever remain inaccessible.
Kurt Gödel Papers,

data.article_summary: 科学家在蒙古博物馆的收藏中发现了一个新恐龙物种——Khankhuuluu mongoliensis，意为“蒙古龙王子”。这一发现重新书写了霸王龙家族进化史。该物种生活在8600万年前，是霸王龙祖先中已知最接近的一支，揭示了霸王龙从侏罗纪时期的小型猎食者演化为强大巨兽的过程。新物种重约750公斤，展示了霸王龙强大咬合力的早期进化特征，如鼻骨结构。这一发现帮助修订了霸王龙的演化谱系，并显示出通过当时连接西伯利亚和阿拉斯加的陆桥，这些恐龙曾在北美和亚洲之间迁徙，推动了不同霸王龙群体的演化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于恐龙最新研究动态的讨论，特别是关于恐龙羽毛和皮肤覆盖物的争议

不同观点：
• **pamelafox**：分享了一本书，建议通过该书了解过去20年有关恐龙的研究，特别是关于恐龙羽毛的研究。作为家长，她觉得有必要对恐龙知识有更多了解。

• **stavros**：对恐龙是否具有羽毛表示困惑，指出一些恐龙化石显示出皮革状覆盖物，而非羽毛。他询问当前科学界最好的猜测是什么，并提出哪些现代动物具有类似的皮革状覆盖物。

• **nashashmi**：提出自己的理论，认为霸王龙主要以爬行姿势活动，以地面的小型食物为食，类似于现代的鬣蜥。

• **rco8786**：提出一个假设，认为许多“新发现”的恐龙实际上只是已知恐龙在不同生命阶段的形态。

补充讨论：
• **HelloUsername**：简单提到了一篇文章的链接，但没有展开讨论。

• **tmtvl**：对恐龙插图表示赞赏，并提出对非鸟类恐龙羽毛触感的疑问，表现出对恐龙外观细节的兴趣。

争议焦点：
• 恐龙的覆盖物：stavros对恐龙羽毛的普遍观点表示怀疑，提出了恐龙化石显示皮革状覆盖物的问题，引发了对恐龙真实外观的好奇和讨论。

重要论据和例子：
• pamelafox提供了关于恐龙羽毛研究的书籍作为参考。
• nashashmi的理论基于对恐龙姿势和饮食习惯的重新想象。
• rco8786的假设基于对恐龙生命周期和形态变化的思考。

这些观点共同展现了公众对恐龙研究进展的关注以及对恐龙生物学特征的持续兴趣和猜测。

44327163.article_content:
New species of dinosaur discovered that 'rewrites' T.rex family tree
12 June 2025
Share
Save
Victoria Gill
Science correspondent, BBC News
Share
Save
Masato Hattori
An artist's impression of Khankhuuluu mongoliensis, the newly discovered tyrannosaur ancestor
Scientists have discovered a new species of dinosaur - in the collection of a Mongolian museum - that they say "rewrites" the evolutionary history of tyrannosaurs.
Researchers concluded that two 86 million-year-old skeletons they studied belonged to a species that is now the closest known ancestor of all tyrannosaurs - the group of predators that includes the iconic T.rex.
The researchers named the species Khankhuuluu (pronounced khan-KOO-loo) mongoliensis, meaning Dragon Prince of Mongolia.
The discovery,
published in Nature,
is a window into how tyrannosaurs evolved to become powerful predators that terrorised North America and Asia until the end of the reign of the dinosaurs.
Darla Zelenitsky
While there are beautiful, complete fossils that give us a clear picture of T.rex (like the one pictured) its earlier ancestors are more mysterious
"'Prince' refers to this being an early, smaller tyrannosauroid," explained Prof Darla Zelenitsky, a palaeontologist from the University of Calgary in Canada. Tyrannosauroids are the superfamily of carnivorous dinosaurs that walked on two legs.
The first tyrannosauroids though were tiny.
PhD student Jared Voris, who led the research with Prof Zelenitsky, explained: "They were these really small, fleet-footed predators that lived in the shadows of other apex predatory dinosaurs."
Khankhuuluu represents an evolutionary shift - from those small hunters that scampered around during the Jurassic period - to the formidable giants, including T.rex.
Julius Csotonyi
An artist's impression of the newly-discovered dinosaur
It would have weighed about 750kg, while an adult T.rex could have weighed as much as eight times that, so "this is a transitional [fossil]," explained Prof Zelenitsky, "between earlier ancestors and the mighty tyrannosaurs".
"It has helped us revise the tyrannosaur family tree and rewrite what we know about the evolution of tyrannosaurs," she added.
The new species also shows early evolutionary stages of features that were key to the tyrannosaurs' tyranny, including skull anatomy that gave it a strong jaw. Jared Voris explained: "We see features in its nasal bone that eventually gave tyrannosaurs those very powerful bite forces."
The evolution of such powerful jaws allowed T.rex to pounce on larger prey, and even bite through bone.
Tyrannosaur's last meal was two baby dinosaurs
Fossil reveals 240 million year-old 'dragon'
Solving the mystery of a dinosaur mass grave
The two partial skeletons that the team examined in this study were first discovered in Mongolia back in the early 1970s. They were initially assigned to an existing species, known as Alectrosaurus, but when Mr Voris examined them, he identified the Tyrannosaur-like features that set it apart.
"I remember getting a text from him - that he thought this was a new species," recalled Prof Zelenitsky.
Riley Brandt/University of Calgary
PhD student Jared Voris and Prof Darla Zelenitsky examine a tyrannosaur fossil
The fact that this group of dinosaurs were able to move between North America and Asia - via land bridges that connected Siberia and Alaska at the time - also helped them to find and occupy different niches.
Mr Voris explained: "That movement back and forth between the continents basically pushed the evolution of different tyrannosaur groups" over millions of years.
Prof Zelinitsky added: "This discovery shows us that, before tyrannosaurs became the kings, they were princes."

Dinosaurs
Evolution

data.title: Marble Blast
data.author: sunday_serif
data.article_summary: 《Marble Blast》是一款由GarageGames开发的游戏，玩家需操控一颗大理石球，在充满动态平台和危险障碍的卡通场景中滚动，收集强化道具以提升速度、跳跃或飞行能力，目标是以最快时间抵达终点并收集所有隐藏宝石。游戏包含多种奖励道具如超级速度、超级跳跃等，以及各种危险如风扇、陷阱门和地雷。玩家还可以查看全球排行榜和最佳成绩。游戏使用Torque游戏引擎，并由Marble Blast团队开发。游戏代码可在GitHub上获取。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Marble Blast及其相关游戏的体验、评价和改进建议

不同观点：
• **对游戏的怀旧与个人经历**  
  - [LanceH] 提到自己为儿子制作自定义地图的经历，并描述了一个现实中的蛋糕装饰活动，将游戏与现实生活结合。
  - [tronium] 分享了自己在5岁时玩Marble Blast Gold的经历，尤其是对某些关卡的深刻印象，表达了对游戏的怀旧情感。

• **推荐其他类似的游戏**  
  - [darthcircuit] 推荐了一个基于Xbox 360版本的逆向工程移植版Marble Blast Ultra，并提到其在Steam Deck上的体验，强调了原生手柄支持对年长玩家的便利。
  - [mdtrooper] 则推荐了另一个类似的游戏Neverball，展示了社区中存在的多样化游戏选择。

• **关于特定关卡和游戏功能的询问**  
  - [smithstreet] 询问了是否存在Xbox 360版本中的"Black Diamond"关卡，显示出对特定游戏内容的关注。
  
• **用户自制的游戏分享**  
  - [archerx] 分享了自己制作的滚球游戏，提供了链接邀请其他人体验，展示了社区中的创造力。

补充讨论：
• **游戏操作问题的反馈**  
  - [Savageman] 提出了游戏中相机视角不跟随转动的问题，表示这使得游戏无法正常进行，寻求解决方案。
  - [n8cpdx] 回应了关于操作的问题，指出游戏实际上有触控控制，并表示这些控制效果不错。

• **对游戏质量和改进的评价**  
  - [Apreche] 对游戏质量给予了积极评价，认为虽然不及Super Monkey Ball，但差距不大。
  - [jbverschoor] 对游戏进行了幽默评价，将其称为"Marble Drift"以表达对游戏体验的感受。
  - [spapas82] 提出了对游戏在移动设备上运行以及使用手机陀螺仪控制球的期望，显示出对游戏跨平台和操作方式改进的需求。

• **意外操作问题**  
  - [01HNNWZ0MV43FF] 描述了一次意外关闭标签页的经历，虽然带有幽默成分，但也暗示了游戏中某些操作提示可能不够明显。

争议焦点：
• **游戏的操作体验问题**，尤其是相机视角不跟随转动，影响了部分用户的游戏体验，是讨论中较为突出的争议点。

Overview
Roll your marble through a rich cartoon landscape of moving
platforms and dangerous hazards. Along the way find
power ups to increase your speed, jumping ability or flight
power, and use them to collect the hidden gems and race to
the finish for the fastest time.
Basic Controls
The marble can be moved forward, back, left and right by pressing
,
,
and
, respectively. Pressing
causes the marble to jump, and pressing
uses whatever powerup you currently have available. All movement is relative to view direction.
Camera Controls
The camera direction can be changed by moving the mouse or by pressing
,
,
or
.  In order to look up and down freely with the mouse, hold down
. You can turn free look on always from the Mouse pane of the Control Options screen.
Goals
Start Pad - this is where you start the level.
End Pad - roll your marble here to end the level.
Gems - if a level has gems, you must pick them all
up before you can exit.
Bonus Items (1/2)
Super Speed PowerUp - gives you a burst of speed.
Super Jump PowerUp - gives you a big jump up.
Shock Absorber PowerUp - absorbs bounce impacts.
Super Bounce PowerUp - makes you bounce higher.
Bonus Items (2/2)
Gyrocopter PowerUp - slows your fall in the air.
Time Travel - takes some time off the clock.
Gravity Modifier - Changes the direction of "down"
- the new down is in the direction of the arrow.
Hazards (1/2)
Duct Fan - be careful this doesn't blow you away!
Tornado - it'll pull you in and spit you out.
Trap Door - keep moving when you're rolling over
one of these.
Hazards (2/2)
Bumper - this'll bounce you if you touch it.
Land Mine - Warning!  Explodes on contact!
Oil Slick - you won't have much traction on these
surfaces.
About GarageGames
GarageGames is a unique Internet publishing label for
independent games and gamemakers.  Our mission is to
provide the independent developer with tools, knowledge,
co-conspirators - whatever is needed to unleash the creative
spirit and get great innovative independent games to
market.
About the Torque
The Torque Game Engine (TGE) is a full featured AAA
title engine with the latest in scripting, geometry, particle
effects, animation and texturing, as well as award winning
multi-player networking code.  For $100 per programmer,
you get the source to the engine!

data.title: Excalidraw+ Is Now SoC 2 Certified
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: Excalidraw+ 获得了 SOC 2 认证，以简化安全合规流程。他们使用 Vanta 来连接服务并修复合规差距，编写了大量政策，实施了零信任生产访问，升级了技术栈，进行了渗透测试，并评估了所有供应商。最终，他们通过了 SOC 2 Type I 认证，正在进行 Type II 认证。SOC 2 是一种安全和合规框架，分为 Type I（检查系统和政策是否存在）和 Type II（检查政策是否长期有效）。尽管政策编写是最繁琐的部分，但大多数安全措施他们早已实施，只是需要正式记录。未来可能还会追求 GDPR 或 ISO 27001 认证。这一过程帮助他们建立了更安全的运营基础。

All posts
Excalidraw+ is SOC 2 compliant
Published
June 18, 2025
by
Milos Vetesnik
TL;DR: Our SOC 2 Journey
We got tired of endless security questionnaires, so we got SOC 2 certified to make things smoother for everyone.
The process:
Used Vanta to connect our services and fix compliance gaps
Wrote a ton of policies
Implemented zero-trust production access
Upgraded our tech stack (Nx, Infisical, monitoring, VPN, etc.)
Did penetration testing
Evaluated all vendors
Result:
Passed SOC 2 Type I 🎉
In progress:
Type II
Next:
maybe GDPR, maybe ISO 27001 (depends on demand)
Most of the security stuff we were already doing, SOC 2 just forced us to write it down officially.
Why SOC 2
At some point, every company reaches the phase where
"we promise we're doing things securely"
just doesn't cut it anymore. We were getting tired of filling out endless security questionnaires, the kind of stuff that can easily live in a proper trust center.
It's one thing to say,
"We use MFA, we encrypt stuff, we care about your data,"
but it hits different when a third party auditor confirms we're actually doing it by the book.
And since our team is still fairly small, we figured it was the right time to get our practices locked in early.
If you're wondering how SOC 2 works or planning to get certified yourself, this post aims to shed some light.
What is SOC 2?
SOC 2 is a security and compliance framework created by the AICPA. It defines how companies should handle customer data using five criteria: security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy.
There are other frameworks, such as ISO 27001, and in the long run, it pays out to get that one too, depending on what your customer base is, but starting with SOC 2 is never a bad idea. It's widely recognized by US companies, less complex than ISO 27001, and builds a solid security foundation to build upon.
There are two flavors of SOC 2:
SOC 2 Type I
checks that your systems and policies exist at a point in time. Basically, whether you have the right setup.
SOC 2 Type II
looks at whether those policies work over time. Think of it as, "cool, but do you really follow through?"
We've completed
SOC 2 Type I
(🎉) and we're already working on Type II.
The Journey
Before you start the certification audit itself, you need to make sure you're in compliance to begin with. If you're young and brave, you can read up on the
criteria requirements
directly from AICPA without using any third-party services to help get going, but such a document doesn't hold your hand or tell you what you need to do. We do not recommend it.
Instead, we looked for services that can get you set up and going easily (well, easier). They help you centralize compliance docs, security workflows, audits, risk monitoring, and all the other things you definitely don't want to be keeping up to date with instead of shipping your product. We narrowed the list down to Drata and Vanta, and in the end, went with Vanta as most of the services and providers we use already had an integration there.
Once you plug all your services in (for us, this meant Vercel, GCP, DigitalOcean, GitHub, among others), Vanta runs a check to see what needs fixing.
Anything without an existing integration, you need to track manually. Sometimes you need to supply evidence in the form of screenshots, so keep your "receipts" at hand! You can do this in Google Drive or elsewhere, but we built this stuff into our internal admin dashboard. It takes a little bit of work upfront, but it pays off long-term and keeps everything nice and organized.
Vanta also helps you introduce secure workstation policies, such as requiring disk encryption, screen locks, and the use of password managers across your entire team. Not exactly groundbreaking stuff, but useful and necessary, and trying to roll that out on our own would have been a nightmare.
The upside for us was that we got a bird’s eye view of our team: who has access to what, whether MFA was enabled, and so on.
Doing all that was a bit overwhelming at first, but once we got the hang of it, it was surprisingly manageable.
The toughest (or let's say, the most annoying) part by far was the policies. You need a ton of them: "Code of Conduct," "Human Resource Security Policy," "Access Control Policy," "Operational Security Policy," and more. Vanta provided some boilerplate templates to get us started, but we still had to tailor them for our company, especially since we're remote-first. Finding the balance between keeping our startup vibes and introducing more rigid and structured processes was key.
Actually implementing those policies was easier for us, as we had already been doing most of these things without them being written down, but there were still some processes that needed updating or technical changes that needed implementing. This can be time-consuming, especially when you're also actively developing a product concurrently. The key is to carve out some dedicated time for this, taking on tasks o

data.author: alomaki
data.article_summary: 作者Jithin Sankar在项目中遇到一个性能问题：每次移动价格滑块时，获取机器学习模型响应需要15秒。由于资源限制，无法通过硬件解决。为在4天内完成计算，作者设计了一种优化方案：利用高斯分布原理，重点计算滑块中间值（高频区域）而减少两端计算。通过预计算约三分之一的战略性价格点，作者将总计算时间从6.9天缩短至2.3天，成功在周末完成任务并顺利通过项目演示。

主要讨论点：计算时间过长以及可能的优化方案

不同观点：
• ViscountPenguin：质疑为什么要花费15秒来计算价格到销售的映射，认为不需要如此多的计算量。同时，不认为客户的滑块点击会遵循正态分布，预期人类会更倾向于在极端点（如开始和结束）操作滑块。

• stephenbez：建议滑块以0.10或0.05的增量移动，以避免用户困惑。
• judahmeek：奇怪于为何不使用最近的缓存值，同时对使用高斯频率表示赞赏，并建议基于初始结果拟合函数。
• conductr：分享自己的经验，通过多线程同时运行多个计算来缩短总时间，但未聚焦于提高单个计算速度。
• Sophira：质疑为何使用机器学习模型，认为这只是计算问题。
• poulpy123：批评这是对客户的欺骗。
• goloroden：认为忽略部分问题不是解决问题，而是提出了一种变通方法。
• ch33zer：询问为何不进行并行预计算。
• sebmaynard：提出正态分布和蒙特卡罗模拟可能达到类似效果，并分享相关链接。

• alomaki：分享自己解决7天计算问题的经验，但未详细描述解决方案。

补充讨论：
• 正态分布的适用性是一个争议焦点，多数评论者认为不适用于描述用户滑块点击行为。
• 提高计算效率的多种可能方案被提出，包括增加增量大小、预计算和线性插值、多线程并行计算等。
• 对实际模型的细节和计算复杂性存在疑问，特别是为何需要如此长的计算时间。
• 有人质疑使用机器学习模型的必要性，认为简单的计算或预计算可能足够。

44329964.article_content:
How I Solved a 7-Day Calculation Problem in a weekend
Jithin Sankar
Follow
3 min read
·
3 days ago
--
Listen
Share
In a previous project, my team was building a SaaS application. The scenario was this: we had a slider for setting a price, from $0.00 to $10.00. When you moved the slider, the app would show you the projected sales for that price. The slider input was combined with two other attributes, Region and SKU name.
The problem was performance. Each time the slider moved, it would take a full 15 seconds to get a response from the ML model. We knew better hardware could fix it, but we had serious resource constraints due to budget issues.
The obvious solution was to
pre-compute and cache
(I built a pypi package for it) all the possible values. Let’s look at the numbers.
We had 10 SKUs, 4 regions, and the slider had two-decimal precision ($0.00, $0.01, …, $9.99, $10.00), which is 1,001 steps.
The total number of combinations would be:
10 SKUs x 4 regions x 1,001 price points = 40,040 requests.
If each request takes 15 seconds, the total time would be:
40,040 x 15 seconds = 600,600 seconds. That’s about
6.9
days.
Our demo was in
4
days.
6.9 days
was not feasible.
So, I thought, let’s do it this way: let’s pre-compute just the odd values, like $0.01, $0.03, and so on.
The probability of the person doing the demo hitting a price with an odd number of cents is 50%. This meant 50 out of 100 times, it would read from the pre-computed cache and give results instantaneously. For the rest, we’d have to wait. During the demo, our team member could surely rig this by picking a cached value, but if the client wanted to play with the values themselves, the whole team would be in trouble. A 50% chance of failure was a risk, but we could go further.
There was one thing I had observed during all our demo trials: when people move a slider, they almost always try to be in the middle. I have never seen anyone working on the extreme ends, like a number near zero or ten.
I remembered this from my engineering days at the College of Engineering, Trivandrum. It’s called the Normal Distribution, or Gaussian distribution. It’s based on the idea that data near the mean (the average) is more frequent than data far from the mean.
A normal distribution curve
The basic idea: most events happen in the middle, fewer at the edges.
Gaussian distribution in this scenario
I figured I could apply some “Gaussian sampling” here (I made up the term, then checked on the internet and saw it exists, so I felt I was on the right path). The idea was to take more values from the middle of the range with high precision (two decimal places) and, as I moved toward the ends of the slider, take fewer values with less precision.
Let’s say I aimed to compute roughly 1/3rd of the total values, but strategically chosen. The new math looked like this:
10 SKUs x 4 regions x ~333 strategic price points x 15 seconds = ~199,800 seconds.
This is 55.5 hours, or about
2.3 days
.
I started the computation script on a Friday night, and by Monday morning, it was ready.
As expected, during the demo, the demonstrator put the slider somewhere in the middle. That value was cached and showed the result instantaneously. Fortunately, the client didn’t have any unexpected options to try. All went well.
I wasn’t lucky. I trust my numbers.

• mylesp：批评文章作者没有考虑更简单的解决方案，建议增加增量大小或预计算每5美分并进行线性插值。
• thom：将此问题归为初级工程师的错误，认为他们没有事先寻求建议。
• curtisf：询问实际模型为何需要15秒计算，认为在只有40条需求曲线且每条曲线参数较少的情况下，计算时间不应如此长。
• stephenbez：建议滑块以0.10或0.05的增量移动，以避免用户困惑。
• judahmeek：奇怪于为何不使用最近的缓存值，同时对使用高斯频率表示赞赏，并建议基于初始结果拟合函数。
• conductr：分享自己的经验，通过多线程同时运行多个计算来缩短总时间，但未聚焦于提高单个计算速度。
• Sophira：质疑为何使用机器学习模型，认为这只是计算问题。
• poulpy123：批评这是对客户的欺骗。
• goloroden：认为忽略部分问题不是解决问题，而是提出了一种变通方法。
• ch33zer：询问为何不进行并行预计算。
• sebmaynard：提出正态分布和蒙特卡罗模拟可能达到类似效果，并分享相关链接。
• _dain_：认为作者的推理不健全，特别指出正态分布不适用于描述用户滑块操作行为，建议考虑其他分布或拟合方法，并对15秒计算时间表示疑问。
• alomaki：分享自己解决7天计算问题的经验，但未详细描述解决方案。

补充讨论：
• 正态分布的适用性是一个争议焦点，多数评论者认为不适用于描述用户滑块点击行为。
• 提高计算效率的多种可能方案被提出，包括增加增量大小、预计算和线性插值、多线程并行计算等。
• 对实际模型的细节和计算复杂性存在疑问，特别是为何需要如此长的计算时间。
• 有人质疑使用机器学习模型的必要性，认为简单的计算或预计算可能足够。

data.title: Breakthrough cancer test predicts whether chemotherapy will work
data.author: bdev12345
data.article_summary: 英国剑桥大学开发了一种突破性测试，能够通过分析肿瘤DNA结构预测化疗是否有效，帮助患者避免不必要的副作用。该测试在840名不同类型癌症患者数据上进行了试点，能够预测卵巢癌、前列腺癌和乳腺癌化疗的成功率。测试可以准确预测三种常见化疗（铂类、蒽环类和紫杉类）的抗药性，每年惠及近10万英国患者。专家希望该测试能在诊断后用于分类患者，避免无效治疗，推动个性化癌症治疗的发展。研究发表于《自然遗传学》期刊，目前正与制药行业合作推进临床应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：癌症治疗中的不同方法及其效果与副作用

不同观点：
• [looofooo0] 分享了一个具体的癌症研究项目，提到通过DNA测序找到合适的药物组合可以有效杀死癌细胞，但有时因为治疗效果过强导致毒性过大，反而对患者有害。研究人员目前正在尝试平衡治疗剂量与效果，以避免过度毒性，同时让部分晚期患者得以康复。这个观点强调了精准医疗和剂量控制的重要性。

• [jader201] 表示自己对癌症治疗了解不多，但原本以为化疗总是对癌症有效果，只是需要权衡其对癌细胞的作用与对健康组织的伤害。该评论者惊讶于某些癌症类型可能对化疗完全无效，暗示了对化疗局限性的认识不足。

• [melling] 认为化疗仍然是治疗许多癌症的最佳手段，但同时指出我们需要更加努力寻找其他疗法。该观点强调了化疗的必要性，但也指出了其作为“毒害身体”的治疗手段的弊端，呼吁替代疗法的开发。

补充讨论：
• [yread] 和 [mynameisash] 没有发表具体观点，但通过提供相关文献链接（[yread] 提供的自然期刊文章和 [mynameisash] 提供的存档链接）为讨论提供了参考资料，可能暗示了对讨论主题的支持性信息或进一步阅读。

争议焦点：
• 化疗的有效性与副作用之间的权衡是讨论的潜在争议点。一方面，化疗是目前广泛使用的有效手段，但其副作用和局限性也引发了对替代疗法的需求和探索。
• 另一个争议点在于治疗剂量和效果的平衡，尤其是当治疗效果过于显著时可能带来的毒性问题，如何在有效杀死癌细胞和保护患者健康组织之间找到最佳平衡仍是研究重点。

Sarah Knapton

23 June 2025 4:15pm BST
A breakthrough test can successfully predict whether
chemotherapy
will work so patients can avoid needless side effects.
The test, developed by the University of Cambridge, looks at the structure of tumour DNA and forecasts whether it will resist treatment.
It was piloted using data from 840 patients with different types of cancer and found that it could help spot whether treatment was likely to fail for ovarian, prostate and breast cancers.
James Brenton, a professor of ovarian cancer medicine at the Cancer Research UK Cambridge Institute, said: “Sadly, there are too many cases where cancer is resistant to chemotherapy treatment – meaning unpleasant
side effects for the patient
with limited benefit to them.
“Chemotherapy is a mainstay of cancer treatment and saves many lives. Yet in many cases, it has been administered the same way for over 40 years. By understanding who is most likely to respond to it, chemotherapy could become a more tailored treatment across different types of cancer.”
The test can accurately predict resistance to treatment of three common types of chemotherapy – platinum-based, anthracycline and taxane chemotherapy – which are given to nearly 100,000 patients in Britain each year.
Although such treatments can help keep cancer at bay, they are also toxic to healthy cells and can lead to unpleasant side-effects such as fatigue, a weakened immune system, nausea and hair loss.
Recommended
The cancer treatment side effects nobody talks about
Read more
Experts hope tests will be used after diagnosis to classify patients as either “chemotherapy resistant” or “chemotherapy sensitive” to treatments, to avoid giving them therapies that will not work.
Dr Iain Foulkes, the executive director of research and innovation at Cancer Research UK, which helped fund the research, said: “The days of chemotherapy being offered as a ‘one-size-fits-all’ treatment are ending.
“Thanks to this research, we are moving towards a future where
personalised cancer treatment
is an option for many patients. Only by delivering more optimised, successful treatment will more people live longer, better lives, free from the fear of cancer.”
Researchers are now working with the pharmaceutical industry to develop the test and will be applying to regulators for its use in the clinic. They are also developing further tests for other targeted cancer drugs to find out how widely the technology could be used across different cancer types.
Dr Ania Piskorz, the head of genomics at the Cancer Research UK Cambridge Institute and the co-lead author, said: “It was important to us to create a test that could be easily adopted in the clinic, using material we already collect during diagnosis and well-established genomic sequencing methods.
“The test is based on the full DNA sequence that we get from these methods, and we can adapt it to work alongside other genomic sequencing methods that are commonly used to personalise treatment for cancer.”
The study was published in the journal Nature Genetics.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大麻使用对健康的影响及其研究数据的可靠性

不同观点：
• **megaloblasto** 认为论文中提出了很多对结果的质疑理由，例如数据中的偏见和研究中重复样本的问题。不过，他也认为开始获取更多关于大麻使用的数据是有价值的。
• **tolerance** 关注的是健康相关 headlines 可能指向年龄在三四十岁的人群，并开始思考同龄人对健康、饮食、健身和生活方式的自我认知。
• **cluckindan** 对大麻使用与健康风险之间的具体关联表示疑问，尤其是与其他日常压力或尼古丁产品使用相比，并猜测效果可能与大麻中的其他成分（如大麻二酚 CBG）有关。
• **vpShane** 强调生活中的压力是大杀器，认为影响健康的数据可能涉及太多因素（如咳嗽、暴饮暴食、缺乏运动等），数据的解读需要谨慎。
• **SoftTalker** 认为如果大麻是吸食的，其健康风险不令人惊讶，因为另一种吸食的叶子（烟草）也有类似的健康关联。

补充讨论：
• **someothherguyy** 提供了相关研究的链接，但没有详细阐述自己的观点。
• **stemlord** 简单地将大麻使用与 junk food 联系起来，暗示大麻使用可能与不健康饮食习惯有关。

争议焦点：
• 研究数据的可靠性和偏见问题，尤其是数据中可能存在的重复样本和偏见。
• 大麻使用与健康风险之间的具体关联，尤其是与其他日常压力或尼古丁产品使用的比较。
• 大麻使用影响健康的潜在机制，是否与其他成分（如 CBG）有关。

整体来看，讨论主要围绕大麻使用健康风险的科学数据可靠性及其具体影响展开，涉及多种健康因素的复杂交互。

data.title: How fast are Linux pipes anyway?
data.author: keepamovin
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了Linux中Unix管道的性能优化过程，通过逐步改进一个通过管道读写数据的测试程序，将其吞吐量从约3.5GiB/s提升至约35GiB/s。作者使用Linux的`perf`工具对程序进行性能分析，并通过几种方法提升性能，包括使用`vmsplice`和`splice`系统调用、利用大页内存、以及用忙等待替代轮询等。文章详细解释了每一步的优化原理，特别是管道在Linux内核中的实现及其导致的性能瓶颈。最终，作者实现了接近于一个高度优化的FizzBuzz程序的管道速度。本文涉及Linux内核细节，适合对系统性能调优感兴趣的读者。代码可在GitHub上找到，测试环境为Intel Skylake i7-8550U CPU和Linux 5.17。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux与Windows在管道性能上的差异、不同操作系统中高效数据传输方法的比较、splice()函数的长期可行性及安全性问题。

不同观点：
• **Windows与Linux的管道性能差异**：zh3分享了将基于Linux管道的应用程序移植到Windows时遇到的性能问题，指出Windows下管道性能较差，甚至导致系统几乎停滞。尽管在Win10中使用C#有所改善，但性能差距依然显著。

• **Linux中高效的管道数据传输方式**：johnisgood指出，在Linux中，splice()是零拷贝情况下在管道和UNIX socket之间传输数据的最有效方式，性能优于readv()/writev()等其他方法。然而，splice()仅在Linux上可用，而在BSD系统中，readv()/writev()则是更高效的选择。

• **splice()的长期可行性与安全性问题**：aeonik表达了对splice()函数长期支持的担忧，尤其是文章末尾提到的安全问题和ABI（应用程序二进制接口）的不兼容性。同时，aeonik对是否可以通过默认管道配置来强制使用splice()以提升性能表示好奇。

• **Linux中低延迟数据交换方式的探讨**：lukeh提问，在现代Linux中是否存在类似于Solaris的Doors机制，用于低延迟进程间通信，特别是在嵌入式应用中是否存在比AF_UNIX更好的选择。

补充讨论：
• **对文章的推荐**：gigatexal对文章表示赞赏，认为这种技术文章的出现非常难得。gkfasdfasdf则提到该文章曾在其他平台被广泛讨论，并提供了相关讨论链接（Hacker News上的讨论帖）。

• **时间点的提示**：layer8简单提到当前是2022年，可能意在提醒讨论的时间背景。

争议焦点：
• **splice()的长期支持与安全性**：部分用户对splice()的长期可行性表示担忧，特别是其安全性及是否有可能在未来版本中被弃用或修改。

• **Windows与Linux管道性能的差异**：zh3通过实际经验指出Windows管道性能不佳，而johnisgood则详细对比了Linux下不同方法的性能优势，表明Linux在管道性能优化上有更多选择。

How fast are Linux pipes anyway?
In this post, we will explore how Unix pipes are implemented in Linux by iteratively optimizing a test program that writes and reads data through a pipe.
1
We will begin with a simple program with a throughput of around 3.5GiB/s, and improve its performance twentyfold. The improvements will be informed by profiling the program using Linuxâs
perf
tooling
.
2
The code
is available on GitHub
.
Chart showing the performance of our pipe test programs.
The post was inspired by reading
a highly optimized FizzBuzz program
, which pushes output to a pipe at a rate of ~35GiB/s on my laptop.
3
Our first goal will be to match that speed, explaining every step as we go along. Weâll also add an additional performance-improving measure, which is not needed in FizzBuzz since the bottleneck is actually computing the output, not IO, at least on my machine.
We will proceed as follows:
A first slow version of our pipe test bench;
How pipes are implemented internally, and why writing and reading from them is slow;
How the
vmsplice
and
splice
syscalls let us get around some (but not all!) of the slowness;
A description of Linux paging, leading up to a faster version using huge pages;
The final optimization, replacing polling with busy looping;
Some closing thoughts.
Section 4 is the heaviest on Linux kernel internals, so it might be interesting even if youâre familiar with the other topics treated in the post. For readers not familiar with the topics treated, only basic knowledge of C is assumed.
Letâs begin!
This will be similar in style to my
atan2f
performance investigation
, although the program in question will only be useful for learning.
Moreover, we will optimize code at a different level. While tuning
atan2f
consisted in micro-optimizations guided by the assembly output, tuning our pipe program will involve looking at
perf
events and reducing various sorts of kernel overhead.
â©ï¸
The tests were run on an Intel Skylake i7-8550U CPU, and on Linux 5.17.
Your mileage
will
vary, since the Linux internals that power the programs described in this post have been under constant change for the past couple of years, and will probably continue to be tweaked in future releases. Keep reading for more details!
â©ï¸
âFizzBuzzâ is an allegedly common coding interview question.
The details are not relevant to this blog post, but they are explained in the link. I have personally never been asked it, but I have it on good authority that it does happen!
â©ï¸
The challenge, and a slow first version
#
First of all, letâs start with measuring the performance of
the fabled FizzBuzz program
, following the rules laid down by the StackOverflow post:
% ./fizzbuzz | pv >/dev/null
422GiB 0:00:16 [36.2GiB/s]
pv
is âpipe viewerâ,
a handy utility
to measure the throughput of data flowing through a pipe. So
fizzbuzz
is producing output at a rate of 36GiB/s.
fizzbuzz
writes the output in blocks as big as the L2 cache, to strike a good balance between cheap access to memory and minimizing IO overhead.
On my machine, the L2 cache is 256KiB. Throughout this post, weâll also output blocks of 256KiB, but without âcomputingâ anything. Essentially, weâll try to measure the upper bound for programs writing to a pipe with a reasonable buffer size.
4
While
fizzbuzz
uses
pv
to measure speed, our setup will be slightly different: weâll implement the programs on both ends of the pipe. This is so that we fully control the code involved in pushing and pulling data from the pipe.
While we fix the buffer size, the numbers are actually not wildly different if we use different buffer sizes, given that other bottlenecks kick in.

in my
pipes-speed-test
repo
.
write.cpp
implements the writing, and
read.cpp
the reading.
write
repeatedly writes the same 256KiB forever.

reads through 10GiB of data and terminates, printing the throughput in GiB/s. Both executables accept a variety of command line options to change their behavior.

and

. Hereâs a view of the writing end:

data.title: Using an $8 smart outlet to avoid brainrot
data.author: NWChen
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种利用8美元智能插座和脚本避免分心的方法。作者编写了一个后台运行的脚本，定期检查智能插座的状态。该插座带有一个手动开关，并通过WiFi连接，允许通过API查看状态。当插座打开时，脚本会更新`/etc/hosts`文件，屏蔽指定的网站，如Twitter、Instagram等。插座可以插在任何电源插座上，最好离用户较远。这样，当想访问被屏蔽的网站时，必须 physically 起身去关闭插座开关，增加的这一步骤有效阻止了无意识的干扰行为。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何有效控制和管理上网行为，特别是减少社交媒体和分心网站的访问

不同观点：
• **支持使用技术工具干预**：
   - cardanome推荐了"One Sec"应用，通过强制呼吸练习来打断冲动访问，认为这种方法对一些人群有效，尤其是ADHD患者。
   - matt_s建议结合使用智能插座和步行垫，将运动与网站访问挂钩，以促进健康行为。
   - layer8认为使用按键而非开关可以防止用户长时间解除限制，并建议使用Amazon Dash按钮实现此功能。
   - thingsilearned通过定时关闭WiFi来限制夜间上网，结合提醒机制帮助用户逐渐适应。
   - parhamn推荐使用SelfControlApp和iOS的停机功能，通过24小时限制和密码保护来减少分心。
   - warunsl分享了Foqos应用程序结合NFC标签的设置，通过物理方式（NFC标签）限制手机应用的使用。

• **手动技术干预**：
   - neilv使用uBlock Origin手动注释和取消注释网站，认为这种方法足以打破访问习惯，必要时可以考虑小额投资。
   - motbus3通过阻止相关网站的JS和cookies来减少分心，认为自动化工具可以帮助解决习惯问题。
   - kybernetyk通过编辑/etc/hosts文件手动阻止访问分心网站，利用输入密码的麻烦来减少访问冲动。

• **质疑工具的有效性**：
   - dankwizard质疑这些工具的长期有效性，认为缺乏自制力的人即使有了工具也无法坚持使用。

• **其他创意解决方案**：
   - Huxley1对廉价自动化工具在减少心理负担和提高专注力方面的效果感到惊讶，并询问其他人是否有类似经验。
   - maguirre提到使用pihole控制网络，但需要考虑家庭成员的正常使用需求，如优惠券网站。

44346450.article_content:
Using an $8 smart outlet to avoid brainrot
2025-06
I wrote a small
script
that runs in the background, polling for the state of an
$8 smart plug
.
It's got a switch on the side to manually toggle the switch on and off. It connects to WiFi, so you can read the state of the plug via API.
When you turn the switch on, the script updates
/etc/hosts
to effectively block websites of your choosing:
127.0.0.1 www.twitter.com
127.0.0.1 x.com
127.0.0.1 instagram.com
127.0.0.1 youtube.com
127.0.0.1 reddit.com
You can plug the switch into any outlet, ideally one far away from you. Now, whenever I want to visit a website in my blocklist, I have to physically get up and turn off the switch. Alternatively, I could just manually edit
/etc/hosts
, but this additional step adds just enough friction to make me reconsider reflexively distracting myself.
